name: Utah
agency: Utah Department of Public Safety, Driver License Division
permitAge: 15 (handbook p.7; entry-level learner permit valid 18 months). Applicants 15-18 must complete approved driver education before licensing (p.6).

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours with a parent or guardian, 10 after sunset (handbook p.6)
teen.holdPermit: Age 16-17: 6 months; age 18: no holding period but driver education required; 19+: 90 days unless driver education completed (handbook p.7)
teen.nightLimit: Provisional licensed drivers (handbook table: age 16; DLD Teen Driver Restrictions page: 16-17): no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 21+ in front, agricultural work, to/from work, school-sponsored activity, or emergency (handbook p.8)
teen.passengerLimit: First six months of the license (or until 18): immediate family members only, unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the front seat, agricultural work, or emergency (handbook p.8; dld.utah.gov/teen-driver-restrictions/)
teen.phone: All drivers: no handheld texting, reading, dialing, internet, video, photos or data entry. 18+: may talk if the call is connected by voice command. Under 18: phone only for medical emergency, reporting a hazard or crime, or talking with a parent or guardian (handbook pp.58-59).

bac.under21: Not a drop: any measurable alcohol (handbook p.52)

notes: Handbook: Utah Driver Handbook 2026, DLD (PDF created 2026-05-11; includes 'New 2026 Laws' effective May 6, 2026). Printed page = PDF page minus 10. No official Spanish handbook found on dld.utah.gov/resources (a Handbook-Translation video exists).

Knowledge test (dld.utah.gov/written-knowledge-test/): never licensed 50-question closed book; previously licensed 25-question open book. Pass 80% (handbook p.23). Two attempts per day; three per fee.

Translated knowledge test for regular or limited-term license applicants in 13 languages (Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, French, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish with audio; Dari, Somali, Swahili, Tagalog, Tongan, Ukrainian, Vietnamese text), or with a division-approved interpreter. Driving Privilege Card applicants not listed.
First-time Class D applicants must also score 100% on the online Traffic Safety and Trends Exam (handbook p.23).
Left lane is for passing; move right when approached from behind (handbook pp.34, 39).

Move over law (handbook p.77): any stationary vehicle by the highway with flashing hazard lights, not legally parked. Penalty in handbook: 4-hour live defensive driving class within 90 days or 90-day suspension. The $160 fine is from news only.
School bus (handbook p.36): opposite traffic need not stop on a divided highway with 4+ lanes and a median, or on 5+ lanes with a center turn lane.

Left on red (Utah Code 41-6a-305(4)(c)): after a full stop, a driver facing a steady red light may turn right, or turn left from a one-way street into a one-way street, yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

Insurance (Utah Code 31A-22-304): policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025 must carry at least $30,000/$65,000/$25,000 (or $90,000 combined); before that $25,000/$65,000/$15,000. PIP at least $3,000 per person for medical expenses (31A-22-307). The insurance.utah.gov glossary still shows the old limits.
BAC 0.05 from December 2018: handbook front matter says Utah was the first state in the country; HB 155 (2017) changed .08 to .05 in 41-6a-502.
